channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Bearish flag forms as bulls eye 0.8200
item.description: The USD/CHF edges higher by some 0.30% on Wednesday, refreshing ten-day highs of 0.8138, as the uptrend is poised to extend if it clears key resistance levels.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Range trade and upside risk against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/CNH has been confined to a tight range and expect the Dollar to trade between 6.7430 and 6.7530 in the near term.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar firms ahead of a packed session
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) has extended its recovery on Wednesday following a Consumer Price Index (CPI) report that printed in line with forecasts. The US Dollar Index (DXY) has pushed back above the 100.00 mark, and the bid has broadened out against most majors heading into a data-heavy Thursday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG turns bullish, eyes 200-day SMA
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price surges over 1.40% on Wednesday as the latest inflation report in the United States (US) showed that prices are cooling, on its way towards the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) goal of 2%. At the time of writing, the XAG/USD pair trades at $65.53 after reaching a daily high of $66.80.

item.title: Gold price shines above $4,400 as inflation dip fuels Fed relief
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) registers gains of over 1% on Wednesday as US inflation data aligns with estimates, easing the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) task of further tightening monetary policy. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) continues its downward trajectory.

item.title: Japanese Yen stumbles as US Dollar strengthens
item.description: USD/JPY is back around the mid-159.00s area, testing the day's highs after rebounding sharply from a low around the 158.60 level.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Fading bullish momentum puts focus on 1.1500 support
item.description: EUR/USD edges lower on Wednesday, reversing earlier gains as the US Dollar (USD) shrugs off in-line US Consumer Price Index (CPI) data. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1521 after touching an intraday high of 1.1563.

item.title: WTI holds firm as Strait of Hormuz concerns outweigh sharp US inventory build
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil trades in a narrow range on Wednesday as traders weigh a sharp rise in US crude inventories against persistent supply risks in the Middle East. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $82.20 per barrel, hovering near a one-and-a-half-week high.

item.title: British Pound holds near 1.3500 as CPI relief meets Hormuz risk
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) holds firm within familiar levels on Wednesday after the US inflation report was in line with estimates, a relief for the Federal Reserve (Fed), which is laser-focused on tackling higher prices. The GBP/USD pair trades at around 1.3500 after reaching a high of 1.3546.

item.title: Australian Dollar slips as US Dollar steadies post CPI
item.description: AUD/USD is trading near the 0.7070 zone, holding onto a minority of Wednesday's gains after the pair touched a session high near 0.7090.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Strong Singapore growth supports SGD against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts highlight that Singapore’s final Q2 GDP was revised up, lifting H1 growth to 6.1% year-on-year and prompting MTI to raise its 2026 GDP forecast to 4.5–5.5%.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar struggles as political uncertainty overshadows US inflation
item.description: NZD/USD retreats to around 0.5865 on Wednesday at the time of writing, down 0.25% on the day. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains under pressure against the US Dollar (USD), while inflation data from the United States (US) triggers only a limited reaction across the foreign exchange market.

item.title: Cooler inflation buys the Dow Jones Industrial Average nothing
item.description: The July Consumer Price Index (CPI) landed at 12:30 GMT on every line the consensus had written for it, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) has spent the hours since handing back the few minutes of enthusiasm that followed.

item.title: Japanese Yen pares gains against US Dollar as markets digest US CPI
item.description: The Japanese Yen trims its gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday as in-line US CPI data fails to trigger a significant move. At the time of writing, USD/JPY trades around 159.20 after touching an intraday low of 158.58.

item.title: Oil: Tightening supply supports elevated prices – BNY
item.description: BNY notes Crude Oil prices remain elevated as doubts over a US–Iran deal heighten supply concerns.

item.title: Silver jumps more than 2% after US inflation meets expectations
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) accelerates its advance on Wednesday and trades around $66.00 at the time of writing, up 2.18% on the day.

item.title: US Dollar: Bearish momentum extends after CPI – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that July US inflation came in broadly in line with expectations, with headline CPI rising 0.1% m/m and core CPI increasing 0.2% m/m.

item.title: President Trump says US has "total control" of Hormuz
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump used a post on Truth Social to declare that the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday., Trump boasted about the American naval presence near the Persian Gulf, which he described as "a wall of steel".

item.title: Euro steadies against Pound Sterling as traders await UK GDP verdict
item.description: The Euro (EUR) steadies against the Pound Sterling (GBP) on Wednesday, with EUR/GBP trading flat near the 0.8540 zone after two consecutive declines.

item.title: Emerging Markets: Steepening Treasuries curb appeal – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu reports that sovereign bonds from commodity-based EM economies have seen accelerated selling after the Fed decision, despite a weaker Dollar and lower U.S. real yields.

item.title: Gold holds gains above $4,400 after US CPI meets expectations
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends gains above $4,400 on Wednesday as traders digest US inflation data, which came broadly in line with expectations. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,429, up 1.38% on the day.

item.title: British Pound: Improving sentiment supports gains against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report the British Pound (GBP) is posting fractional gains versus the US Dollar (USD) and outperforming G10 peers as improving sentiment supports price action.

item.title: Canadian Dollar steadies as US inflation meets expectations, Oil limits downside
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.3915 on Wednesday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day with a modest decline of 0.06%.

item.title: Pound Sterling retains gains as US CPI trims September Fed hike odds
item.description: GBP/USD trades modestly higher on Wednesday as the US Dollar (USD) comes under mild pressure following the release of the latest US inflation figures. However, the market reaction remains limited as the data broadly matched expectations.

item.title: Brazil: Lula victory could deepen fiscal risks - Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts Brendan McKenna and Dev Ashish outline scenarios for Brazil’s 2026 election, assigning a 65% probability to President Lula winning a fourth term and 30% to Flavio.

item.title: United Kingdom: Resilience tested as data mixed – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley reviews recent United Kingdom (UK) data against Eurozone performance. Foley notes Eurozone Q2 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at 0.4% q/q and a 0.7% UK upturn in the three months to May.

item.title: Oil: Chinese demand recovery could lift prices – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada's (NBC) Jocelyn Paquet analyzes how China’s sharp reduction in petroleum imports helped offset the Middle East supply shock and limit Oil price gains. The July rebound in Chinese imports is highlighted as historically large in percentage terms.

item.title: Euro remains little changed as US CPI fails to surprise the markets
item.description: EUR/USD trades around 1.1550 on Wednesday at the time of writing, up a modest 0.08% on the day.

item.title: Breaking: US CPI inflation softens to 3.4% in July as expected
item.description: Annual inflation in the United States (US), as measured by the change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), declined to 3.4% in July from 3.5% in June, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported on Wednesday. This print came in line with the market expectation.

item.title: IEA forecasts 4.3 million bpd drop in global Oil supply
item.description: The International Energy Agency (IEA) cut its global Oil supply and demand forecasts for 2026 amid shipping disruptions in the Middle East.
